source:
@@U02944@@
And I’m certain that in the months and years you've stored up all kinds of experience.

@@U02946@@
Experience! Smoke in the wind is more like it! Not equal to the mind of man. Confess: what’s known as knowledge isn't worth the knowing.

@@U02948@@
(After a pause.)

@@U02949@@
Yes, I suspected it long ago. I was a fool; and now I see how shallow and silly I am.

@@U02951@@
Glad to hear it. You're talking sense. The first old-timer I’ve known to be reasonable!

@@U02953@@
I’ve searched for buried golden treasures, and come back with dust and ashes.

@@U02955@@
Admit it, that bald head of yours is worth no more than those skulls over there!

@@U02957@@
(Genially.)

@@U02958@@
I trust, my friend, you don’t know how rude you are.

@@U02960@@
To be polite in German is to be a liar. (梅菲斯特 has been inching closer to the proscenium in his wheelchair.)
translation:
@@U02944@@
我确信，在这几个月和几年里，你已经积累了各种各样的经验。

@@U02946@@
经验！风中的烟雾更像了！不等于人心。承认：所谓的知识并不值得了解。

@@U02948@@
（停顿后。）

@@U02949@@
是的，我很久以前就怀疑过。我是个傻瓜；现在我才发现我是多么肤浅和愚蠢。

@@U02951@@
很高兴听到这个消息。你说的是有道理的。我认识的第一个讲道理的老前辈！

@@U02953@@
我寻找过埋藏的黄金宝藏，却带着尘土和灰烬回来。

@@U02955@@
承认吧，你的那个光头根本不比那边的那些头骨值钱！

@@U02957@@
（亲切地。）

@@U02958@@
我相信，我的朋友，你不知道自己有多粗鲁。

@@U02960@@
在德语中，有礼貌就等于说谎。 （梅菲斯特坐在轮椅上慢慢靠近舞台。）
